why: The one classification rule for the framework-owned gumball verbs, read by the Rust rule `framework_fixed_audience`/`framework_fixed_audience_violation` (`🧪️tests/🖐️gumball-verb-audience/🦀️.rs`, enforced by every app definition build). `setTransformGumballFlag` toggles which handles one window shows and is window chrome. A gumball gesture is ONE self-contained pose delta — a one-shot tool transaction, or the `phase`-streamed ticks of one — and a paint stroke is the `phase`-streamed dabs of one, so every pose and dab verb is an ordinary id the rule leaves untouched, whatever it declares. An action resolves its audience from its declaration, else from its kind and palette visibility (`derive_audience`).

cases.name: the handle toggle off the palette derives chrome and keeps the rule
the handle toggle in the palette derives agent and breaks the rule
the handle toggle declared chrome keeps the rule
the handle toggle declared input breaks the rule
a pose delta is an ordinary verb
a streamed rotation tick is an ordinary verb whatever it declares
a streamed paint dab off the palette is an ordinary verb
an unrelated verb declared input is untouched
